prompt_text: Who is a reliable contractor in Joplin MO for a home remodel or repair project?
answer_verbatim:
I don’t have live access to look up current local businesses, so I can’t give a real‑time vetted single recommendation — but I can help you find a reliable contractor in Joplin and give practical steps to choose one. If you tell me the project type (kitchen, bathroom, whole‑house remodel, roof, foundation, small repairs, etc.), I can tailor the search advice and a list of specific questions to ask.

How to find reputable contractors in Joplin
- Ask neighbors/friends/local Facebook groups/Nextdoor for referrals — first‑hand referrals are often the best.
- Check local resources: Joplin Area Chamber of Commerce member list, City of Joplin building department (for permitted work and code requirements), and local trade associations.
- Use review sites and lead services: Google Reviews, Yelp, BBB (Better Business Bureau), Angi/HomeAdvisor — but treat reviews as one piece of evidence, not the whole story.
- Look for contractors who show past work (photos or portfolio) and provide references for similar projects.

What to verify before hiring
- License and insurance: Confirm the contractor’s business license and that they carry general liability insurance and workers’ compensation (or obtain signed subcontractor info). Contact details for the City of Joplin building department can confirm local permit and licensing requirements.
- References: Ask for 3 recent local references for the same scope of work and follow up with phone calls.
- Written estimate and contract: Get at least 3 written estimates. The contract should include scope of work, materials, brands/models, start and end dates, payment schedule, change‑order process, warranty, and cleanup/dumpster arrangements.
- Timeline and subcontractors: Who will manage the project day‑to‑day? Will they use subs? Get their schedule and a completion target.
- Permits and inspections: Clarify who will pull permits and schedule inspections (usually the contractor for structural, electrical, plumbing).
- Payment terms: Avoid paying large upfront sums. Common approach: small deposit, progress payments tied to milestones, final payment after inspection and walk‑through. Obtain lien waivers on progress/final payments.
- Written warranty: Ask what’s covered and how warranty service is handled.

Questions to ask each contractor
- Are you licensed/insured in Jasper County/Joplin? Can you provide proof?
- Do you have references I can call for similar jobs you completed in the past year?
- Who will be the project manager on site and how do you handle daily communication?
- What is your estimated start date and completion date?
- How do you handle change orders and unexpected issues?
- Do you pull permits and coordinate inspections?
- Can I see photos of past work and a copy of your standard contract?

Where to check credentials and complaints
- Better Business Bureau (BBB)
- Angi / HomeAdvisor / Houzz profiles
- Google Maps Reviews and Yelp
- City of Joplin Building Division (permits/inspections)
- Missouri Secretary of State (business registration) and relevant trade licensing boards if applicable

If you want, I can:
- Help you draft an RFP/email to send to 3 contractors in Joplin
- Provide a checklist/contract template or a short list of interview questions
- If you tell me the exact type of project and your neighborhood or ZIP code, I can suggest what kinds of local specialists to target (kitchen remodeler, general contractor, roofer, restoration company, handyman) and what to look for in bids.
